Batch every file, range and symbol you need into ONE `read` call (`path`, `path:A-B`, `path#Symbol`, `#Symbol`, globs); oversized files come back as skeletons you expand by symbol instead of being cut off. `search` hits show their enclosing function/class; `trace` follows callers, callees, references and implementations; `map` orients you in a repo. Bug report: behind trusted proxies, c.ClientIP() returns the proxy's address instead of the client's. With the header `X-Forwarded-For: 20.20.20.20, 30.30.30.30` and 30.30.30.30 configured as a trusted proxy, ClientIP() should return 20.20.20.20. Find and fix the bug in the library code (do not modify tests). Verify with `go test ./...`. When done, reply with a one-line summary of the fix.

Use the speedread MCP tools (read, search, trace, map) to read, search and navigate code; use the built-in tools only to edit files and run commands.

[993-1047] func (c *Context) ClientIP() string
993	// ClientIP implements one best effort algorithm to return the real client IP.
994	// It calls c.RemoteIP() under the hood, to check if the remote IP is a trusted proxy or not.
995	// If it is it will then try to parse the headers defined in Engine.RemoteIPHeaders (defaulting to [X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP]).
996	// If the headers are not syntactically valid OR the remote IP does not correspond to a trusted proxy,
997	// the remote IP (coming from Request.RemoteAddr) is returned.
998	func (c *Context) ClientIP() string {
999		// Check if we're running on a trusted platform, continue running backwards if error
1000		if c.engine.TrustedPlatform != "" {
1001			// Developers can define their own header of Trusted Platform or use predefined constants
1002			if addr := c.requestHeader(c.engine.TrustedPlatform); addr != "" {
1003				return addr
1004			}
1005		}
1006	
1007		// Legacy "AppEngine" flag
1008		if c.engine.AppEngine {
1009			log.Println(`The AppEngine flag is going to be deprecated. Please check issues #2723 and #2739 and use 'TrustedPlatform: gin.PlatformGoogleAppEngine' instead.`)
1010			if addr := c.requestHeader("X-Appengine-Remote-Addr"); addr != "" {
1011				return addr
1012			}
1013		}
1014	
1015		var (
1016			trusted  bool
1017			remoteIP net.IP
1018		)
1019		// If gin is listening a unix socket, always trust it.
1020		localAddr, ok := c.Request.Context().Value(http.LocalAddrContextKey).(net.Addr)
1021		if ok && strings.HasPrefix(localAddr.Network(), "unix") {
1022			trusted = true
1023		}
1024	
1025		// Fallback
1026		if !trusted {
1027			// It also checks if the remoteIP is a trusted proxy or not.
1028			// In order to perform this validation, it will see if the IP is contained within at least one of the CIDR blocks
1029			// defined by Engine.SetTrustedProxies()
1030			remoteIP = net.ParseIP(c.RemoteIP())
1031			if remoteIP == nil {
1032				return ""
1033			}
1034			trusted = c.engine.isTrustedProxy(remoteIP)
1035		}
1036	
1037		if trusted && c.engine.ForwardedByClientIP && c.engine.RemoteIPHeaders != nil {
1038			for _, headerName := range c.engine.RemoteIPHeaders {
1039				headerValue := strings.Join(c.Request.Header.Values(headerName), ",")
1040				ip, valid := c.engine.validateHeader(headerValue)
1041				if valid {
1042					return ip
1043				}
1044			}
1045		}
1046		return remoteIP.String()
1047	}

[993-1047] func (c *Context) ClientIP() string
993	// ClientIP implements one best effort algorithm to return the real client IP.
994	// It calls c.RemoteIP() under the hood, to check if the remote IP is a trusted proxy or not.
995	// If it is it will then try to parse the headers defined in Engine.RemoteIPHeaders (defaulting to [X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP]).
996	// If the headers are not syntactically valid OR the remote IP does not correspond to a trusted proxy,
997	// the remote IP (coming from Request.RemoteAddr) is returned.
998	func (c *Context) ClientIP() string {
999		// Check if we're running on a trusted platform, continue running backwards if error
1000		if c.engine.TrustedPlatform != "" {
1001			// Developers can define their own header of Trusted Platform or use predefined constants
1002			if addr := c.requestHeader(c.engine.TrustedPlatform); addr != "" {
1003				return addr
1004			}
1005		}
1006	
1007		// Legacy "AppEngine" flag
1008		if c.engine.AppEngine {
1009			log.Println(`The AppEngine flag is going to be deprecated. Please check issues #2723 and #2739 and use 'TrustedPlatform: gin.PlatformGoogleAppEngine' instead.`)
1010			if addr := c.requestHeader("X-Appengine-Remote-Addr"); addr != "" {
1011				return addr
1012			}
1013		}
1014	
1015		var (
1016			trusted  bool
1017			remoteIP net.IP
1018		)
1019		// If gin is listening a unix socket, always trust it.
1020		localAddr, ok := c.Request.Context().Value(http.LocalAddrContextKey).(net.Addr)
1021		if ok && strings.HasPrefix(localAddr.Network(), "unix") {
1022			trusted = true
1023		}
1024	
1025		// Fallback
1026		if !trusted {
1027			// It also checks if the remoteIP is a trusted proxy or not.
1028			// In order to perform this validation, it will see if the IP is contained within at least one of the CIDR blocks
1029			// defined by Engine.SetTrustedProxies()
1030			remoteIP = net.ParseIP(c.RemoteIP())
1031			if remoteIP == nil {
1032				return ""
1033			}
1034			trusted = c.engine.isTrustedProxy(remoteIP)
1035		}
1036	
1037		if trusted && c.engine.ForwardedByClientIP && c.engine.RemoteIPHeaders != nil {
1038			for _, headerName := range c.engine.RemoteIPHeaders {
1039				headerValue := strings.Join(c.Request.Header.Values(headerName), ",")
1040				ip, valid := c.engine.validateHeader(headerValue)
1041				if valid {
1042					return ip
1043				}
1044			}
1045		}
1046		return remoteIP.String()
1047	}

data.content: Found the bug: in `validateHeader` (gin.go), the trust check is inverted — it returns the IP when `isTrustedProxy(ip)` is true, so it returns the trusted proxy itself instead of skipping past it.
data.reasoningText:
I'm reconsidering the proxy-trust logic here: the algorithm should walk the IP list from last to first, skipping over trusted proxies and continuing until it finds the first untrusted IP, which represents the real client. The current condition looks backward since it returns the IP when it's trusted rather than skipping it, so I want to trace through an example header to verify.

Testing with "20.20.20.20, 30.30.30.30" and 30.30.30.30 as a trusted proxy confirms the bug — the loop returns the trusted proxy itself as the client IP instead of continuing back to 20.20.20.20. So the fix is to reverse the condition: continue iterating when the current IP is trusted, and only return once we hit an untrusted IP or run out of items, matching the real gin implementation's approach of parsing IPs from the tail of the header and breaking on invalid ones.
